questions.prompt: Humans do not work like a perfect recording device because:
choices: A We see ultraviolet and hear all dog frequencies.
B We sample limited sensations and construct perception—we don't see everything.
C Attention captures 100% of inputs always.
D Smell is unused.
questions.explain: Limited senses and selective attention; not a full recording.

choices: A Identical terms.
B Sensation is input via sensory apparatus; perception is the reintegrated experience we 'see.'
C Perception precedes all sensation always.
D Only ears do perception.
questions.explain: Sensation in; perception after neural reintegration.

choices: A Perfect accuracy on ambiguous objects.
B Seeing meaningful patterns (e.g., faces) in ambiguous stimuli.
C That dual-process theory is false.
D Only color blindness.
A Media exposure never biases probability estimates.
B Vivid examples can warp odds judgments (dual-process/heuristic sense-making).
C Only System 2 ever runs.
D Sharks are irrelevant to realism talks.
questions.explain: Jellyfish movie vividness vs actual odds—heuristic distortion.

choices: A Beliefs and behaviors never conflict.
B Holding conflicting cognitions (I smoke / smoking is bad) creates pressure to resolve.
C Only applies to earthquakes.
D Festinger studied only golf swings.
questions.explain: Smoking example of dissonance between knowledge and behavior.
